Photograph: Mark Large/Shutterstock Mohamed Al Fayed French police raid Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed sexual abuse investigation Arrests made after three properties were searched in relation to inquiry into late businessman David Batty Tue 10 Nov 2026 15.00 EST Last modified on Tue 10 Nov 2026 16.15 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris , in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed. Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office. Another property in Paris and one in Saint-Tropez, both with links to Fayed, were also searched in mid-October. Several of Fayed’s alleged victims were also interviewed by officers from the organised crime division of the Paris prosecutor’s office. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into “allegations of human trafficking committed by an organised group, aggravated pimping committed by an organised group, and rape”. In an email sent to survivors of Fayed’s alleged abuse earlier today, the Metropolitan police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in a coordinated operation with French investigators. The Paris prosecutor’s office said: “Searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed , and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.” The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed, it added. One of the properties that was raided was Castel Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, one of the most exclusive villas on the French Riviera, and where Diana, Princess of Wales , stayed with her sons in the summer of 1997, at the start of her relationship with Fayed’s son, Dodi. The other was Villa Windsor , a former holiday home of the Fayed family. The property in western Paris was previously the family home of Charles de Gaulle, before he was president of France, and King Edward VIII, after his abdication, and his wife, Wallis Simpson. A Met spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France last month and were present during the operation. Campaign groups representing Fayed’s alleged victims called on the Met police to conduct its own searches of the late billionaire’s properties. Co-chairs of Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors, Jen Mills and Lindsay Mason, said: “We want to see the same thoroughness applied to every property where survivors say they were taken or abused, including here in Britain. The searches in Paris and Saint-Tropez must be the beginning, not the end.” A spokesperson for No One Above , a collective of survivors of Fayed’s alleged abuse, said: “The French authorities have put this in the hands of their specialist trafficking unit and their organised crime prosecutors, and are investigating it as trafficking by an organised gang. “The evidence in this case was never confined to Harrods. For two years, the Met has avoided treating it as what France recognised from the outset: organised trafficking by a network. The National Crime Agency should now take over the investigation.” Pelham Spong, who says she was trafficked in Paris on Fayed’s orders in 2008 before being sent to London to be sexually assaulted by him, said she was overjoyed by the French police raids. “Survivors deserve actions, not words,” she added. Last November, she told French investigators from the Central Office for the Repression of Human Trafficking that Fayed, who owned the Ritz hotel in Paris , had forcibly kissed her and offered her a salary of € 65,000 a year if she slept with him. Survivors’ groups say more than 500 women have come forward about abuse that allegedly took place at Harrods, Park Lane, Fulham football club, the Ritz hotel in Paris, and other places owned by Fayed. The Met is investigating 169 victims who have contacted the force directly. The Ritz Paris told Agence France-Presse news agency that it “does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour” and that it was ready “to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities”. https://hvg.hu/tudomany/20261120_antarkt.text: Eddig ismeretlen ősi hegyvonulatot fedezett fel egy nemzetközi kutatócsoport az Antarktisz jege alatt. Az Earth and Planetary Science Letters című folyóiratban közölt tanulmányban az Ausztrál Nemzeti Egyetem (ANU) és a német GFZ Földtudományi Kutatóközpont kutatói olyan hatalmas, ősi hegyvonulatok maradványait azonosították, amelyek a Gondwana szuperkontinens kialakulása során, 650 és 450 millió évvel ezelőtt keletkeztek. A kutatók szerint a hegyvonulatok akkor keletkeztek, amikor az Antarktisz összeütközött Indiával és Afrikával, amit a szakemberek a kontinenst érintő legnagyobb hegyképződési folyamatnak neveztek. Az Antarktisz területének több mint 99,5 százalékát vastag jégtakaró borítja, ami megnehezíti geológiai történetének feltárását. A kontinens múltjának rekonstruálásához a kutatók az antarktiszi kontinentális perem mentén lerakódott üledékekből származó 1712 apró cirkonkristályszemcsét elemeztek. A minták vizsgálatából meg tudták állapítani a kőzetek korát és kémiai összetételét, amelyekből származnak, valamint következtethettek belőle a geológiai folyamatokra is, amelyek során keletkeztek. Egy évtizedenként egyszer előforduló időjárási anomália, a trópusi Csendes-óceán felmelegedése és az abból adódó kelet-antarktiszi havazás lassította átmenetileg az antarktiszi jégtakaró tömegvesztését Ian Campbell, az ANU emeritus professzora, a tanulmány egyik társszerzője rámutatott: „aligha lehetett véletlen, hogy a Föld drámai fejlődési szakasza egybeesik a Föld legfontosabb hegyképződési időszakával, a Gondwana szuperhegységeinek kialakulásával és eróziójával”. A hegységképződés idején jelentek meg az első szilárdvázú élőlények mintegy 539 millió évvel ezelőtt, és 10–30 millió évvel később zajlott le a kambriumi robbanás is, amikor ugrásszerűen megnőtt az állatvilág fajgazdagsága, az ökoszisztémák összetettsége és populációja. A kutatók megállapították, hogy a Gondwana szuperhegységeinek gyors eróziója csökkentette a légköri szén-dioxid-szintet, növelte az oxigénkoncentrációt, és tápanyagokkal látta el az óceánokat, ami kedvező feltételeket teremtett az élővilág elterjedéséhez és az evolúció felgyorsulásához. A felfedezés hozzájárul a kontinens földtani múltjának és a földi élet evolúciójának alaposabb megismeréséhez. Ha máskor is tudni szeretne hasonló dolgokról, lájkolja a HVG Tech rovatának tudományos felfedezésekről is hírt adó Facebook-oldalát .

https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/25/russ.text: Russia launched scores of drones at energy and civilian targets across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, killing at least seven people in six regions, authorities said.The attack involved 112 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, of which 88 were shot down or neutralised, Ukraine's air force said.One person was killed in Bila Tserkva in Kyiv region, where the strike damaged critical infrastructure, an Epicentr shopping centre and a Nova Poshta postal branch, local authorities said.One person was killed and seven injured in Kharkiv region after a strike hit a minibus on a highway, regional governor Oleh Synehubov said. Two people aged 76 and 69 were killed and another wounded in Sumy region.Two people were killed in Odesa region on Tuesday evening — a 41-year-old and a 17-year-old — and one person was killed and three wounded in Zhytomyr region. Casualties were also reported in Chernihiv and Donetsk regions.Russian forces struck a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Poltava region, the acting head of the company Serhiy Fedorenko said.A fire broke out and the facility suspended operations. "This is not the first such attack and, unfortunately, not the last," Fedorenko said, adding that Russia was deliberately targeting gas production "to deprive Ukrainians of heat in winter."Energy facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region were also hit, triggering emergency power cuts across several districts.A significant number of consumers lost power in Zaporizhzhia region, Zaporizhzhyaoblenergo head Andriy Stasevskyi said. More than 9,000 customers were left without electricity in Odesa region following Tuesday evening's attacks, regional governor Oleh Kiper said.The energy company DTEK reported a large-scale strike on one of its thermal power plants, causing serious damage and forcing it to stop generating electricity. DTEK did not specify the location, noting it was the third large-scale strike on its plants in November.Ukraine strikes Russian refineries and airbaseUkrainian drones simultaneously struck three Russian oil refineries overnight, hitting plants in Samara and Rostov regions, according to Ukrainian monitoring sources.Two refineries in Samara region — the Kuibyshev and Syzran plants, both part of Rosneft — were struck, with fires breaking out at both facilities.Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the attack but did not name the facilities, saying one person was killed, power had been cut in several districts and a number of schools would operate on an adjusted schedule.Regional authorities said 145 drones were shot down over the Samara region. Euronews could not independently verify these claims.The Syzran refinery has a processing capacity of 8.5 million tonnes of oil per year and produces petrol, diesel, aviation kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen.The Kuibyshev refinery has a primary processing capacity of 8.8 million tonnes per year. Ukraine last struck the Syzran plant on 15 September. The Kuibyshev refinery was also struck that month.The third refinery struck overnight was the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region. Regional governor Yuri Slyusar confirmed the attack, saying a combined strike of more than 50 drones and missiles lasted six hours before the plant suspended operations.Russian oil refining volumes have fallen by an estimated 45% since late October, according to analysts.Ukraine's General Staff also reported overnight strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, which it described as one of Russia's key aviation facilities and the base from which aircraft carrying Kinzhal missiles launch strikes on Ukrainian cities.According to Kyiv's military, three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged and would be unable to fly "for some time".Ukraine destroyed a span of the road section of the Crimean Bridge last week, halting car traffic, though train services have been restored.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, describing deep strikes inside Russia as "long-range sanctions".Ukraine attacked the bulk carrier Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, claiming it transported military cargo. The following day it struck the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Zelenskyy confirmed the warship had been sunk.On Tuesday, Russia's Vladimir Putin threatened Ukraine with retaliation for its strikes on refineries and complained that Kyiv had not heeded calls from US President Donald Trump to halt attacks on oil processing facilities.Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was prepared to stop striking Russian refineries only if Moscow halted its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
